rejected.title: Displaying data
card: Categorical data
A two-way table counts how many people fall in each pair of categories. A segmented bar chart shows the same counts as percentages, so groups of different sizes can be compared.
Numerical data
A dot plot puts one dot per value and suits small sets. A histogram groups values into equal intervals and suits large sets.
Stem plot
A stem plot is also for numerical data. It splits each value into a stem and a leaf, so every value stays visible. If the stem is tens, then 3 | 4 means 34.
Log scale
On a log base 10 scale, 1, 10, 100 and 1000 are equally spaced. Each step is ×10. It suits data spread over several powers of ten.
rejected.remember: Categories: two-way tables and segmented bar charts. Numbers: dot plots, stem plots and histograms.

a.q: Which display lets you read back every original value in a data set?
a.why: A stem plot shows each value as a stem and a leaf. A histogram groups values into intervals, so the exact values are lost.
a.clue: Which one splits each value into two parts?

b.q: Ava asks 40 Year 11 and 120 Year 12 students if they work part-time. Which display best compares the percentage who work in each year?
b.why: Year group and working or not are categories, and the groups differ in size, so percentages give a fair comparison. A segmented bar chart shows percentages. A histogram, dot plot and stem plot are for numerical data, not categories.
b.clue: Is the answer to Ava's question a number or a category?

a.q: A teacher wants a numerical display where every original value can still be read back. Which display should she use?
a.why: A stem plot keeps each value, because the stem and leaf together give the whole number. A histogram only counts values in each interval, so the exact values are lost. The other two displays are for categories, not numerical values.
a.clue: Think about what a histogram bar tells you about the values inside it.
